title: O'Fallon, Illinois man convicted of shooting at U.S. Marshals - NewsBreak
text:
By Kevin S. Held ,
7 hours ago
EAST ST. LOUIS, Ill. – A federal jury convicted an O’Fallon, Illinois, man Thursday for shooting at U.S. Marshals who attempted to serve him with an arrest warrant.
Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Illinois said Earl Frank, 57, was found guilty of one count of assault on a federal officer, count of discharge of a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence and one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm.
Court documents state that on June 6, 2025, federal agents attempted to arrest Frank at a motel room at the Royal Budget Inn in East St. Louis. Frank was considered a fugitive after cutting off his ankle monitor in St. Louis in July 2024 while he was on supervised release.
Deputy U.S. Marshals knocked on Frank's motel door and announced themselves three times. When a deputy marshal used a keycard to open the motel door, Frank fired a .380 pistol at law enforcement.
[sailthru_widget name="Sailthru Widget Block" sailthru_list="Breaking News" title="Breaking News"] Frank was arrested after a brief standoff. Marshals found the pistol and a spent .380 shell casing in motel room. A box of .380 ammunition was located inside Frank's car, which was parked outside his room.
Because Frank has a prior felony conviction, he's not allowed to own or possess a firearm or ammo.
Federal prosecutors have not disclosed a sentencing date. Frank faces up to 20 years for assault on a federal officer, a minimum of 10 years for discharge of a firearm and up to 15 years for possession of a firearm.
Frank was previously charged as part of a sweeping federal investigation into drug trafficking linked to the Sinaloa Cartel in Mexico.
